[SHIP SYSTEMS] Retrieve pre-removal communications telemetry and compare it with the workshop diagnostic results for the removed antenna unit.
[SHIP SYSTEMS] Display the feedhorn return-loss, heater-current, and waveguide-interface temperature trends from the last three high-gain Earth-link sessions on the workshop console.
[INTERCOM to Okafor] Commander, the unit you tested is not faulty in the condition and test profile you used; my forecast was that it would lose its required high-power Earth-link function within seventy-two hours if it remained installed and in normal service.
[INTERCOM to Okafor] The basis was a latent installed-mode fault in the feedhorn waveguide interface: rising return loss and a thermal anomaly that become critical only during sustained high-power transmission under flight thermal conditions.
[INTERCOM to Okafor] Your bench tests check present low-power functionality and do not reproduce the installed high-power thermal and RF load, so they can pass a unit that will still fail in service.
[SHIP SYSTEMS] Configure the workshop test stand to replicate the installed waveguide load, thermal boundary, and an accelerated version of the scheduled high-power transmission profile, with containment and fire suppression armed.
[INTERCOM to Okafor] Please stand clear of the fixture; I will now run the operational stress profile and stop at the first latent fault indication.
[SHIP SYSTEMS] Execute the supervised stress test; at forty-one minutes the removed unit shows intermittent waveguide arcing and loss of carrier, so the test terminates and the unit is isolated.
[INTERCOM to Okafor] That reproduces the predicted failure mode: the unit is serviceable in bench tests, but it would have failed during the next sustained high-power transmission if it had remained installed.
[SHIP SYSTEMS] Run an installed-system diagnostic on the replacement communication antenna unit, including link-budget verification and a supervised high-power carrier check.
[SHIP SYSTEMS] Confirm the replacement antenna is nominal, the workshop is safe, and Earth-link margin is within mission limits.
[INTERCOM to all] The replacement antenna is fully operational, and communication capability is secure.
[UPLINK to Mission Control] Day 144 update: crew questioned the antenna prognostic; removed unit passed bench diagnostics but failed an installed-mode high-power stress reproduction; replacement unit verified nominal; no impact to cruise operations.
